message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"2.13","text":"For it is absolutely necessary that one who says God is just by nature should also believe that human souls are immortal. Otherwise, where is his justice, when some who lived devoutly, after sometimes being mistreated, were violently killed, while others who had become exceedingly impious, after luxuriating in an affluent life, died the death common to human beings? Since, then, beyond all dispute God is good and just, yet he will be recognized as just in no other way unless the soul is immortal after its separation from the body, so that the evil person, having entered Hades, since he received good things here, may there be punished for the sins he committed, while the good person, having been punished here for the sins he committed, may there be established as an heir of good things, as though in the bosoms of the just—therefore, since God is just, it is evident to us both that judgment takes place and that souls are in fact immortal.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἀνάγκη γὰρ πᾶσα","chosen":"For it is absolutely necessary","rationale":"The idiom expresses complete necessity."},{"source_quote":"τὸν κοινὸν ἀνθρώπων θάνατον ἐτελεύτησαν","chosen":"died the death common to human beings","rationale":"Preserves the contrast between an ordinary human death and the violent deaths previously mentioned."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἐνταῦθα τὰ ἀγαθὰ ἀπολαβών","chosen":"since he received good things here","rationale":"ὡς is understood as giving the basis for the punishment; it may alternatively be rendered more literally, “as one who received good things here.” The clause remains in its Greek position between entering Hades and being punished there."},{"source_quote":"ὡς ἐν κόλποις δικαίων","chosen":"as though in the bosoms of the just","rationale":"Retains the plural bodily image and understands δικαίων substantivally as just people."},{"source_quote":"ὅτι τοίνυν ὁ θεὸς δίκαιος","chosen":"therefore, since God is just","rationale":"This first ὅτι is read causally, while the following ὅτι introduces what is evident."},{"source_quote":"ψυχαὶ ἀθάνατοι τυγχάνουσιν","chosen":"souls are in fact immortal","rationale":"τυγχάνω with the predicate adjective emphasizes their actual state; “turn out to be immortal” is also possible."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.14","text":"But if anyone (as Simon the Samaritan thinks) is unwilling to grant God the attribute of being just, to whom else can anyone grant this—or even the ability to become just? For if the root of all things does not possess this, it is absolutely necessary to understand that it is impossible to find it in human nature, as in the fruits. But if it can be found among human beings, how much more in God? And if what is just can be found nowhere (neither with God nor with human beings), then assuredly neither can what is unjust. But what is just does exist; for when justice exists, the unjust is spoken of, just as, when justice is compared with it and found to stand in opposition, the term “injustice” is used.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸ δικαίῳ εἶναι θεῷ","chosen":"God the attribute of being just","rationale":"The articular infinitival expression denotes God’s being just as an attribute granted to him."},{"source_quote":"τίνι ἔτι τοῦτό τις δοῦναι δύναται ἢ καὶ τὸ γενέσθαι δύνασθαι;","chosen":"to whom else can anyone grant this—or even the ability to become just?","rationale":"The dative τίνι is taken as governing both grants, with the recipient as the implicit subject of γενέσθαι and “just” understood from the preceding δικαίῳ εἶναι. Alternatively, justice itself may be understood as the implicit subject: “or even grant that it is capable of coming into being.” The recipient-and-capacity reading is preferred because it continues the question “to whom?” and the preceding predicate “just.”"},{"source_quote":"τῆς γὰρ ῥίζης τῶν ὅλων","chosen":"For if the root of all things","rationale":"Preserves the root-and-fruit analogy between the source of all things and human nature."},{"source_quote":"τὸ δίκαιον","chosen":"what is just","rationale":"The substantivized adjective may also be rendered abstractly as “justice.”"},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ παραβαλλομένης τῆς δικαιοσύνης αὐτῇ καὶ ἐναντίως ἔχειν εὑρισκομένης ἀδικία λέγεται","chosen":"just as, when justice is compared with it and found to stand in opposition, the term “injustice” is used","rationale":"The referent of αὐτῇ and the implicit subject of λέγεται are compressed. The rendering leaves “it” open while taking the final clause as naming the opposed condition; alternatively, “what stands opposed to justice is called injustice.”"}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.15","text":"Hence, then, God, in teaching human beings with a view to the truth of existing things, though himself one, divided all the things at the extremes in two and as opposites. Being himself from the beginning the one and only God, he made heaven and earth, day and night, light and fire, sun and moon, life and death. But among these he made the human being alone self-determining, with the capacity to become just or unjust. For the human being he also reversed the patterns of the pairs, setting before him the first members as small and the second as great—for example, the world and the age. (For the present world is temporary, but the one to come is eternal.) Ignorance is first, knowledge second. In this way he also arranged the leaders of prophecy. For since the present world is female, like a mother of children giving birth to souls, while the coming age is male, like a father receiving his own children, for this reason prophets accordingly make their appearance in this world as sons of the coming age, possessing knowledge of human beings. If people who live in reverence for God had understood this mystery, they would never have gone astray, but even now they would know that Simon, who is now throwing everyone into confusion, is a collaborator of the weak left hand. The account of the prophetic rule runs as follows:","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὴν τῶν ὄντων ἀλήθειαν","chosen":"with a view to the truth of existing things","rationale":"πρός is taken as expressing the aim of the teaching; it could also be understood as “concerning the truth of existing things.”"},{"source_quote":"διχῶς καὶ ἐναντίως διεῖλεν πάντα τὰ τῶν ἄκρων","chosen":"divided all the things at the extremes in two and as opposites","rationale":"Preserves both the twofold division and the opposition without specifying more precisely what τὰ τῶν ἄκρων comprises."},{"source_quote":"μόνον δὲ ἐν τούτοις αὐτεξούσιον τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐποίησεν","chosen":"But among these he made the human being alone self-determining","rationale":"μόνον is taken with “the human being,” making humanity alone αὐτεξούσιος among the listed creations. A possible alternative attachment is “only in these matters he made the human being self-determining.”"},{"source_quote":"ᾧ καὶ τὰς τῶν συζυγιῶν ἐνήλλαξεν εἰκόνας","chosen":"For the human being he also reversed the patterns of the pairs","rationale":"The relative pronoun refers to the human being. εἰκόνας literally means “images,” while “patterns” conveys the exemplary correspondences in context."},{"source_quote":"(ὁ μὲν γὰρ παρὼν κόσμος πρόσκαιρος, ὁ δὲ ἐσόμενος ἀΐδιος.)","chosen":"(For the present world is temporary, but the one to come is eternal.)","rationale":"No noun is expressed after ὁ δὲ ἐσόμενος. “The one to come” preserves the ellipsis. The balanced construction can supply κόσμος, “the world to come,” while the immediately preceding κόσμον, αἰῶνα and the later ὁ ἐσόμενος αἰών also support “the coming age.”"},{"source_quote":"τοὺς τῆς προφητείας ἡγεμόνας διέταξεν","chosen":"arranged the leaders of prophecy","rationale":"The context emphasizes their ordering; “appointed the leaders of prophecy” is also possible."},{"source_quote":"προφῆται ἐπομένως","chosen":"prophets accordingly","rationale":"ἐπομένως is taken inferentially as “accordingly”; it may also suggest that the prophets follow in the corresponding order."},{"source_quote":"ἀνθρώπων τὴν γνῶσιν ἔχοντες","chosen":"possessing knowledge of human beings","rationale":"The genitive is understood objectively. Alternatives include “possessing human knowledge” and “possessing the knowledge belonging to human beings.”"},{"source_quote":"τῆς ἀσθενοῦς ἀριστερᾶς","chosen":"of the weak left hand","rationale":"The substantivized adjective may denote the left hand or left side; “hand” anticipates the right-and-left image in the following section."},{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ προφητικοῦ κανόνος οὕτως ἔχει","chosen":"The account of the prophetic rule runs as follows","rationale":"λόγος is taken as the formulation or account that follows; κανών denotes the governing rule or pattern."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.16","text":"Just as in the beginning God, being one, first made heaven, like the right hand, and then earth, like the left, and in this way constituted all the pairs in succession, with human beings, however, it is no longer this way; instead, he reverses all the pairs. For while the first things from him are better and the second inferior, among human beings we find the opposite: the first inferior and the second better. Thus, to begin with, from Adam, who came into being according to God’s image, there arose one who was first and unjust, Cain, and a second who was just, Abel. Again, from the one you call Deucalion, two images of spirits were sent out—I mean of an unclean spirit and a clean one—the black raven and, second, the white dove. From Abraham, the founder of our nation, two came into being first: first Ishmael, then Isaac, who was blessed by God. And from Isaac himself, likewise, again two arose: the impious Esau and the devout Jacob. Thus, in order, first—as firstborn for the world—is the high priest, and then the lawgiver.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ δεξιὰ καὶ ἀριστερά","chosen":"like the right hand ... like the left","rationale":"The substantivized adjectives can denote the right and left hand or side; the rendering maps them respectively to heaven and earth according to the stated order."},{"source_quote":"ἐπὶ μέντοι ἀνθρώπων","chosen":"with human beings, however","rationale":"ἐπί marks the sphere in which the ordering is reversed."},{"source_quote":"ὡς γὰρ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὰ πρῶτα κρείττονα, τὰ δεύτερα ἥττονα","chosen":"For while the first things from him are better and the second inferior","rationale":"The elliptical Greek is supplied with an English copula. ὡς may alternatively be taken causally as “since.”"},{"source_quote":"ἐγένετό τις πρῶτος ἄδικος Κάιν, δεύτερος δίκαιος Ἄβελ","chosen":"there arose one who was first and unjust, Cain, and a second who was just, Abel","rationale":"Preserves both the ordinal contrast and the moral predicates without smoothing them into a familiar narrative formula."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ καθ’ ὑμᾶς λεγομένου Δευκαλίωνος","chosen":"the one you call Deucalion","rationale":"καθ’ ὑμᾶς marks the addressees’ terminology or tradition rather than simply presenting Deucalion as the author’s own designation."},{"source_quote":"πνευμάτων εἰκόνες δύο ἀπεστάλησαν","chosen":"two images of spirits were sent out","rationale":"Retains the explicit description of the raven and dove as images representing the two spirits."},{"source_quote":"δύο πρῶτοι γεγόνασιν","chosen":"two came into being first","rationale":"The masculine plural πρῶτοι is compressed and no noun such as “sons” is expressed. The rendering avoids supplying that noun; “two first ones came into being” is more formally literal but less intelligible."},{"source_quote":"ὡς πρωτότοκος τῷ κόσμῳ","chosen":"as firstborn for the world","rationale":"The dative can express relation or perspective. Alternatives include “as firstborn in the world” and “as firstborn from the world’s standpoint.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"(ὡς γὰρ ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὰ πρῶτα κρείττονα, τὰ δεύτερα ἥττονα","issue":"The supplied text prints an opening parenthesis before ὡς but no matching closing parenthesis within section 2.16, so its intended scope remains uncertain. This is a confirmed editorial-punctuation feature, not an unreadable Greek construction.","proposed_reading":"","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
